findings.finding: PhysX applies force and contact constraints during a simulation interval. Separating the preceding applied-force impulse from measured momentum change can expose an unexplained residual, but normal-force telemetry alone cannot identify tangential friction. Motion and dwell are useful separate landing diagnostics.
findings.confidence: high for interval bookkeeping; limited for causal attribution
findings.relevance: Additional no-outage seeds 401 and 503 violate final support position and are already displaced when the original supervisor disarms
findings.direction_alignment: Inspect horizontal control and contact before proposing another controller change
findings.opportunity_or_risk: A residual can be mistaken for a friction measurement and an offline predicate for an alternate simulated landing; both must remain explicitly descriptive
findings.engineering_cost: Ten related landing-analysis features, retained-recording reconstruction and browser validation; no simulation runtime change
findings.roadmap_delta: AL-025 adds the requested landing contact lab over the full retained AL-024 matrix
findings.verification_needed: Independent interval arithmetic, phase boundaries, interrupted contacts, strict data contracts, original failure preservation and actual paired 3D demonstration

overall_recommendation: Use retained physics to locate motion before contact, between contact and disarm, and after disarm. Require a separately predeclared physics experiment for any later supervisor change.
evidence_gaps: No separately recorded tangential contact impulse
No causal identification from passive replay
No counterfactual trajectory from offline readiness
Ideal attitude/contact supervision and AL-010 yaw refinement remain limitations
